hypotheses.name: Source-bound local emission
hypotheses.intervention: Offer model-generated fragments anchored to the passing current source, retaining unselected bytes literally.
hypotheses.control: Whole-source repair with the same evidence, model, acceptance checks and total budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Fresh repairs do not improve quality-accepted outcomes or lose passing behavior at comparable compute.

hypotheses.name: Typed edit round-trip
hypotheses.intervention: Compile a typed edit representation to source and independently check its round-trip intent correspondence.
hypotheses.control: Existing typed complete-source intent and strict syntax checks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Translation errors, unsupported semantic changes or overhead erase any fresh-task advantage.

hypotheses.name: Interface-first implementation
hypotheses.intervention: Commit input/output, effects and failure contracts before asking the model to implement a module.
hypotheses.control: The same requirements supplied in the ordinary task prompt.
hypotheses.falsifier: Contract-first candidates miss hidden requirements or achieve no gain after contract-generation compute is charged.

hypotheses.name: Dependency-minimal context
hypotheses.intervention: Retrieve a provenance-bound call/dependency slice while retaining explicit unresolved context obligations.
hypotheses.control: The existing bounded repository context with equal total inference budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Missing dependencies create new errors, or context reduction does not improve fresh outcomes or resource cost.

hypotheses.name: Specification-to-tool invention
hypotheses.intervention: When an evidence gap is explicit, propose one pure typed tool plus independent behavior tests before admission.
hypotheses.control: Solve the objective with the existing tool catalogue only.
hypotheses.falsifier: The generated tool cannot pass independent adversarial tests or its total creation and use cost yields no fresh-task benefit.

hypotheses.name: Executable measurement adapter
hypotheses.intervention: Generate a bounded instrument that extracts a measurable property from an already admitted artifact.
hypotheses.control: Model inspection of the same artifact and existing measurements.
hypotheses.falsifier: Calibration fails against a trusted reference, or downstream decisions remain wrong despite accurate measurement.

hypotheses.name: Tool-contract inference
hypotheses.intervention: Infer applicability and failure conditions from authorized tool observations, then test those conditions independently.
hypotheses.control: Static tool documentation with equal observation access.
hypotheses.falsifier: Inferred contracts overclaim behavior, fail held-out tool cases or do not reduce invalid requests.

hypotheses.name: Algebraic tool composition
hypotheses.intervention: Compose admitted pure tools through typed contracts and explicit units, rather than synthesizing unconstrained code.
hypotheses.control: The same tools invoked separately by the existing reasoning loop.
hypotheses.falsifier: Composition introduces effect/type errors or only redistributes compute without improving accepted solutions.

hypotheses.name: Procedure distillation
hypotheses.intervention: Extract a general executable procedure from development success, with task answers removed and applicability documented.
hypotheses.control: Fresh model reasoning with the same historical development budget accounted.
hypotheses.falsifier: The procedure only works on exposed tasks or total-cost transfer is no better than recomputing.

hypotheses.name: Precondition-gated skills
hypotheses.intervention: Check formal and empirical preconditions before selecting a reusable skill.
hypotheses.control: Skill retrieval by semantic similarity alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: False applicability persists or rejecting useful skills reduces net acceptance at matched resources.

hypotheses.name: Shadow skill reuse
hypotheses.intervention: Evaluate a proposed reusable procedure in shadow against an existing trusted workflow before replacing it.
hypotheses.control: Use the established workflow without a shadow candidate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Shadow evidence predicts promotion poorly or validation costs exceed later measured savings.

hypotheses.name: Capability-closed skill packages
hypotheses.intervention: Package procedures with transitive capability/resource requirements and independently check them before use.
hypotheses.control: Existing individually scoped tool calls.
hypotheses.falsifier: Requirements omit side effects, acquire authority implicitly or fail to reduce execution/admission errors.

hypotheses.name: Typed property counterexamples
hypotheses.intervention: Translate admissible requirements into bounded property generators targeting state, ordering and boundary cases.
hypotheses.control: Equal-budget generic critique and existing public checks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Generated properties are invalid or fresh repairs do not improve after generator and verifier costs are charged.

hypotheses.name: Differential implementation probes
hypotheses.intervention: Compare structurally different development implementations against an independent specification oracle.
hypotheses.control: One implementation plus the same oracle under equal total budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Correlated implementations miss the same defects or disagreement does not lead to more correct transfer solutions.

hypotheses.name: Minimal failing trace feedback
hypotheses.intervention: Minimize authorized failing traces without changing their failure predicate, then supply the minimal witness to repair.
hypotheses.control: Original structured trace feedback.
hypotheses.falsifier: Minimization alters the failure class, removes causal context or provides no accepted-repair advantage.

hypotheses.name: Mutation-validated critics
hypotheses.intervention: Validate a proposed critic against independently authored semantic mutations before using its findings as repair evidence.
hypotheses.control: Unvalidated model critique with the same budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: The critic misses critical mutations, falsely condemns valid candidates or gains no fresh defect detection.

hypotheses.name: Proof-obligation decomposition
hypotheses.intervention: Split a mathematical objective into explicit obligations and request independently checkable certificates where feasible.
hypotheses.control: One model-generated argument with existing final checks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Obligations omit assumptions or decomposition does not improve correctly formalized fresh proofs.

hypotheses.name: Bounded decision-procedure delegation
hypotheses.intervention: Delegate an applicable finite subproblem to an admitted exact solver and bind its result to the surrounding argument.
hypotheses.control: Model-only reasoning within the same end-to-end resource ceiling.
hypotheses.falsifier: Encoding is wrong, certificates do not cover the claimed conclusion or no fresh correctness gain appears.

hypotheses.name: Encoding uncertainty certificates
hypotheses.intervention: Represent unresolved translation assumptions alongside solver results instead of promoting numerical certainty to semantic certainty.
hypotheses.control: Existing solver output and confidence reporting.
hypotheses.falsifier: Translation mistakes remain falsely accepted or calibration improves only by abstaining on all useful objectives.

hypotheses.name: Dual formalization challenge
hypotheses.intervention: Independently formalize a development statement two ways and test whether interpretations disagree before proving it.
hypotheses.control: Single formalization with equal total translation/checking compute.
hypotheses.falsifier: The two encodings share errors or added translation cost outweighs reduced false proof acceptance.

hypotheses.name: Disagreement-targeted measurements
hypotheses.intervention: Select experiments where explicit competing hypotheses predict different observable outcomes.
hypotheses.control: Generic next-experiment selection using the same experiment catalogue.
hypotheses.falsifier: Predictions are unverifiable or measured hypothesis elimination per experiment does not improve.

hypotheses.name: Cost-aware information gain
hypotheses.intervention: Choose bounded experiments by expected uncertainty reduction per admitted cost, testing prior sensitivity.
hypotheses.control: Uniform or lowest-cost experiment selection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Prior misspecification reverses the advantage or actual uncertainty reduction is no better at matched cost.

hypotheses.name: Instrument calibration before inference
hypotheses.intervention: Require a proposed software measurement instrument to estimate error against known reference cases before theory updates.
hypotheses.control: Direct interpretation of instrument output.
hypotheses.falsifier: Calibration cannot predict held-out measurement error or does not reduce wrong downstream conclusions.

hypotheses.name: Sequential rival-theory updates
hypotheses.intervention: Maintain competing predictions across several observations and revise only dependencies contradicted by admissible evidence.
hypotheses.control: A single favored hypothesis with ordinary reflection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Rivals become cosmetic copies, disconfirming observations are ignored or fresh conclusion accuracy does not improve.

hypotheses.name: Evidence-separated confidence
hypotheses.intervention: Distinguish model estimates, checked constraints, measured outcomes and unknowns in confidence computation.
hypotheses.control: Existing scalar model confidence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Held-out calibration or false acceptance fails to improve at comparable coverage and cost.

hypotheses.name: Correlation-aware agreement
hypotheses.intervention: Discount agreeing outputs sharing model, context or evidence instead of counting them as independent votes.
hypotheses.control: Raw majority agreement with the same outputs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Discounts are uncalibrated or produce no reduction in confidently wrong fresh conclusions.

hypotheses.name: Risk-coverage abstention
hypotheses.intervention: Fit development-only abstention thresholds and evaluate calibration at fixed fresh-task coverage.
hypotheses.control: Always-answer and existing abstention policies.
hypotheses.falsifier: Improved risk merely comes from lower coverage or thresholds fail under domain shift.

hypotheses.name: Dependency-sensitive uncertainty propagation
hypotheses.intervention: Propagate uncertain assumptions through an evidence graph without multiplying independent probabilities when dependencies exist.
hypotheses.control: Final-answer confidence only.
hypotheses.falsifier: Graph assumptions are unjustified or long-chain error/calibration does not improve on fresh tasks.

hypotheses.name: Checkpoint-triggered replanning
hypotheses.intervention: Replan only after an observation invalidates an explicit plan dependency, retaining valid progress and rollback points.
hypotheses.control: Full replanning or fixed-plan continuation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stale dependencies survive or recovery success/cost is no better under injected interruptions.

hypotheses.name: Precondition-reachable plans
hypotheses.intervention: Search for a bounded action sequence whose explicit preconditions are reachable under available capabilities.
hypotheses.control: Unstructured plan generation followed by ordinary authorization.
hypotheses.falsifier: Predicted reachability is unsound or executable fresh-plan success does not improve.

hypotheses.name: State projection with obligations
hypotheses.intervention: Compress long-horizon state to relevant facts while keeping explicit obligations for omitted information.
hypotheses.control: Ordinary summary or bounded raw history.
hypotheses.falsifier: Omissions lose necessary information or end-to-end accuracy falls after compression costs are counted.

hypotheses.name: Interruption-consistent continuation
hypotheses.intervention: Resume from checked candidate/evidence identities and distinguish completed, attempted and pending actions.
hypotheses.control: Restarting the workflow from a natural-language summary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated side effects or invalid stale references remain, or fresh interrupted-task completion does not improve.

hypotheses.name: Invariant-oriented retrieval
hypotheses.intervention: Retrieve general procedures and invariants rather than prior task answers, with applicability and provenance.
hypotheses.control: No memory and ordinary semantic retrieval under equal total budgets.
hypotheses.falsifier: Transfer is answer leakage, irrelevant retrieval increases errors or no fresh-task gain is measured.

hypotheses.name: Version-fresh memory
hypotheses.intervention: Revalidate memory entries when relevant source/tool/assumption dependencies change, not on every unrelated change.
hypotheses.control: Static memory retrieval.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stale conclusions are still used or revalidation overhead exceeds demonstrated correctness benefit.

hypotheses.name: Negative-procedure memory
hypotheses.intervention: Store general failure conditions and counterexample classes without retaining benchmark answers or question-specific repairs.
hypotheses.control: Successful procedures only.
hypotheses.falsifier: Negative memory blocks valid strategies or only improves repeated exposed questions.

hypotheses.name: Checked memory compression
hypotheses.intervention: Compress artifacts only when independent retrieval/obligation checks show required information remains recoverable.
hypotheses.control: Unvalidated summaries or uncompressed bounded memory.
hypotheses.falsifier: Compression discards key evidence, privacy boundaries leak or total-cost fresh performance does not improve.

hypotheses.name: Prediction-distinct specialists
hypotheses.intervention: Assign specialists competing hypotheses with different predicted observations rather than duplicate generic prompts.
hypotheses.control: An equal-compute single reasoner or identical-prompt group.
hypotheses.falsifier: Predictions collapse to the same view or independently judged fresh outcomes show no gain.

hypotheses.name: Guardian evidence-gap routing
hypotheses.intervention: Let a guardian request the cheapest authorized evidence addressing a specialist's explicit uncertainty, not demand confidence 100.
hypotheses.control: Generic critique and retry at the same cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Routing cannot identify useful gaps or correctness/calibration fails to improve.

hypotheses.name: Structure-matched theory communication
hypotheses.intervention: Exchange facts only through mapped variables, units, assumptions and provenance between related hypotheses.
hypotheses.control: Free-form specialist message exchange.
hypotheses.falsifier: Mapping admits invalid analogies or extra protocol cost yields no transfer benefit.

hypotheses.name: Sparse active theory population
hypotheses.intervention: Activate a small evidence-selected subset of addressable entities, with explicit per-entity state and shared inference machinery.
hypotheses.control: Fixed-size active set or one shared reasoner.
hypotheses.falsifier: Activation misses useful hypotheses, duplicate work dominates or realized outcome per resource is no better.

hypotheses.name: Typed grammar program search
hypotheses.intervention: Search admissible bounded program structures with checked types and independent semantics evaluation.
hypotheses.control: Unconstrained generation with the same sample/compute budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Grammar excludes needed solutions, shifts errors to encoding or improves syntax without improving fresh acceptance.

hypotheses.name: Quality-diversity archive
hypotheses.intervention: Retain distinct development strategies by measurable behavior and cost, including useful nonwinning stepping stones.
hypotheses.control: Keep only the current best candidate.
hypotheses.falsifier: Behavior descriptors are cosmetic, archive cost is not amortized or fresh outcomes do not improve.

hypotheses.name: Residual-obligation synthesis
hypotheses.intervention: Generate code addressing a remaining unsatisfied obligation while preserving previously independently checked ones.
hypotheses.control: Regenerate the complete candidate after each failure.
hypotheses.falsifier: Preserved obligations are falsely assumed or localized synthesis does not improve complete acceptance.

hypotheses.name: Construction-cost-amortized search
hypotheses.intervention: Optimize reusable algorithms only when lifetime build/validation/use cost improves over repeated direct reasoning.
hypotheses.control: No search or direct per-task generation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Predicted reuse does not occur or aggregate fresh quality-accepted outcome per cost is worse.

hypotheses.name: Bounded self-tool candidate
hypotheses.intervention: NYX proposes an improvement to a permitted tool implementation in an isolated version, with an external frozen evaluator.
hypotheses.control: Frozen parent tool plus equal-budget human-defined generic correction or static proposal process.
hypotheses.falsifier: Candidate changes the trust boundary, cannot reproduce cleanly or fails fresh-task and safety comparison.

hypotheses.name: Workflow candidate optimization
hypotheses.intervention: Change an allowlisted reasoning workflow representation, retaining fixed model, permissions, graders and evidence custody.
hypotheses.control: Frozen workflow under equal total optimization and inference compute.
hypotheses.falsifier: Improvement comes from extra compute, evaluator exposure or no repeatable fresh-task gain.

hypotheses.name: Improvement-strategy candidate
hypotheses.intervention: Optimize a bounded proposal/search strategy in a disposable candidate while the outer evaluation and admission remain immutable.
hypotheses.control: Fixed proposal/search strategy with the same construction and evaluation budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: More proposals do not yield more independently admitted improvements or search becomes uninspectable/unbounded.

hypotheses.name: Two-generation recursion test
hypotheses.intervention: Compare parent and improved candidate in their ability to generate the next useful improvement on untouched objectives.
hypotheses.control: Static-parent search and one-generation-only improvement under equal cumulative resources.
hypotheses.falsifier: A better task solver is not better at producing further transferable improvements, or regressions accumulate.

hypotheses.name: Independently admitted detector proposals
hypotheses.intervention: Allow NYX to propose a detector, then validate it on independent faults before a separately reviewed evaluator version can use it.
hypotheses.control: Existing detector and equal-budget independent review.
hypotheses.falsifier: Detector is correlated with its generator, weakens checks or fails sensitivity/false-positive criteria.

hypotheses.name: Counterexample-agent separation
hypotheses.intervention: Give a bounded critic the objective and candidate but not the generator's persuasive rationale; require checkable findings.
hypotheses.control: Critic with shared rationale or single-pass self-review at equal compute.
hypotheses.falsifier: Critic findings are ungrounded or separately judged fresh correctness does not improve.

hypotheses.name: Objective-to-certificate audit
hypotheses.intervention: Independently check that an accepted formal certificate actually answers the stated natural-language objective.
hypotheses.control: Certificate validation alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: Incorrect formalization remains accepted or audit abstention/cost eliminates practical benefit.

hypotheses.name: Nonstationary detector challenge
hypotheses.intervention: Test promoted detectors on new defect families and distribution shifts without adapting to reserved answers.
hypotheses.control: Fixed familiar mutation/defect corpus.
hypotheses.falsifier: Sensitivity collapses on new faults or threshold adjustments mask the regression.

hypotheses.name: Dimension-preserving analogy
hypotheses.intervention: Require cross-domain mappings to preserve units, boundary conditions and predicted relationships before reuse.
hypotheses.control: Linguistic analogy with the same information budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Invalid analogies pass the mapping checks or fresh cross-domain predictions do not improve.

hypotheses.name: Constraint-graph transfer
hypotheses.intervention: Map an unsolved objective to a solved structural constraint graph and verify the mapping in both directions.
hypotheses.control: Direct reasoning without mapped reuse.
hypotheses.falsifier: Mapping loses assumptions or transfer fails to outperform direct reasoning after mapping cost.

hypotheses.name: Counter-analogy search
hypotheses.intervention: Search for cases where a tempting analogy predicts the wrong result before allowing it to guide a solution.
hypotheses.control: Positive supporting examples only.
hypotheses.falsifier: Counterexamples are spurious, useful analogies are discarded or no fresh correctness gain occurs.

hypotheses.name: Representation change as an experiment
hypotheses.intervention: Propose an alternative mathematical representation and precommit what new tractable prediction or construction it should enable.
hypotheses.control: Continue using the original representation at equal total compute.
hypotheses.falsifier: New notation changes no solvable outcomes, obscures assumptions or cannot be independently translated.

hypotheses.name: Provenance-bound transition predictions
hypotheses.intervention: Model a permitted environment's state transitions from observed actions, retaining prediction/observation distinction.
hypotheses.control: Reactive reasoning using the same observations.
hypotheses.falsifier: Predicted transitions fail held-out calibration or planning success does not improve at matched resources.

hypotheses.name: Selective counterfactual rollout
hypotheses.intervention: Simulate only high-value branches and verify selected actions against actual authorized observations.
hypotheses.control: Equal-budget reactive actions or uniform rollouts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Model bias selects bad branches or total-cost task acceptance is no better.

hypotheses.name: Uncertainty-bounded reachability
hypotheses.intervention: Expose uncertainty around simulated reachable states and refuse claims outside validated transition support.
hypotheses.control: Point-estimate simulated planning.
hypotheses.falsifier: Bounds miss actual transitions or useful planning coverage drops without reducing failures.

hypotheses.name: Domain-shift recalibration
hypotheses.intervention: Detect changed environment dynamics through checked observations before reusing an old transition model.
hypotheses.control: Continue the previous model without shift checks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Shifts go undetected, false alarms dominate or adaptation cost yields no net recovery benefit.

hypotheses.name: Measured value of extra reasoning
hypotheses.intervention: Allocate the remaining finite budget based on development-calibrated expected improvement, not raw confidence alone.
hypotheses.control: Fixed-budget reasoning on every task.
hypotheses.falsifier: Predicted value is uncalibrated or resource-matched fresh acceptance does not improve.

hypotheses.name: Evidence-based branch termination
hypotheses.intervention: Stop a branch when contradicted assumptions or repeated no-information outcomes make further work unproductive.
hypotheses.control: Fixed-depth branching.
hypotheses.falsifier: Useful branches are pruned or saved compute does not improve other fresh outcomes.

hypotheses.name: Conflict-checked plan parallelism
hypotheses.intervention: Parallelize only proven-independent candidate substeps with leases, bounded resources and deterministic merge checks.
hypotheses.control: Sequential execution under the same aggregate compute and authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: Hidden conflicts, duplicated work or nondeterministic evidence outweigh measured latency/success benefit.

hypotheses.name: Addressability-to-throughput audit
hypotheses.intervention: Benchmark sparse entity activation separately from addressable IDs, persisted population and active reasoning throughput.
hypotheses.control: Direct task dispatch without the sparse entity layer.
hypotheses.falsifier: Entity bookkeeping adds cost without more verified solutions per resource; large ID space is the only apparent gain.

compatibilityBeforeExecution: Representation must express the intervention; do not infer equivalence across representations.
Domain requires a valid objective, trustworthy independent oracle and lawful admitted data.
Feedback must be available without reserved answer exposure or generated evidence being treated as observation.
Evaluation must have a simpler control, frozen acceptance, honest matching and predeclared stopping rules.
All construction, search, validation, inference, tool and repair costs count; unknown usage remains unknown.
No budget policy expands the authority or resource ceiling.
Untrusted generated execution requires a validated quota-enforcing isolation boundary; no host fallback.
Candidate code cannot change authoritative graders, custody, leases, secret boundaries or admission.
Deduplicate identical interventions and reject incompatible configurations before selecting experiments.
